questions.question: What is a Go module and what does go.mod contain?
questions.title: Go Module And Go Mod
questions.direct_answer: A module is a versioned collection of packages (one go.mod). go.mod declares the module path, Go version, and dependencies with versions. It's the unit of versioning and dependency resolution.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: A module is a versioned collection of packages (one go.mod). go.mod declares the module path, Go version, and dependencies with versions. It's the unit of versioning and dependency resolution.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The file:

```go
module example.com/mymod

go 1.22

require github.com/google/uuid v1.6.0
```

Executed: after go mod init example.com/mymod and adding a dependency, go mod tidy produced exactly this (verified).

The three sections: module path (the identity — the import prefix for the module's packages), the Go version (language/toolchain floor), and the requires (each dependency with its version).

What a module IS: a directory tree with go.mod at the root. All packages under it share the module path as their import prefix: example.com/mymod/pkg/parser imports as that path. One go.mod per module; no nesting (that's the workspace's job).

The versioning: the module version tags (v1.2.3) map to git tags — the module system resolves imports to specific versions, pinned by go.mod, verified by go.sum.

The common commands:
go mod init <path> — creates go.mod
go mod tidy — add/remove requires to match imports
go mod download — fetch into the cache
go mod graph — the dependency graph
go get github.com/pkg/dep@v1.2.3 — add/update a specific version

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M[go.mod] --> P[module path]
    M --> V[go version]
    M --> R[requires + versions]
    M --> S[go.sum — integrity hashes]
    S --> CACHE[module cache — verified]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The module path semantics: it's not just a name — it's the URL (usually) that go get uses to find the source, AND the import prefix. The three path families: public (github.com/org/repo — fetched by URL), private (with GOPRIVATE + auth), and local-only (any path, used with replace directives or workspaces).

The version selection algorithm: Minimal Version Selection — Go picks the MINIMUM version that satisfies all requirements (unlike other systems that pick the MAXIMUM). A dependency required at v1.2.0 by one package and v1.4.0 by another gets v1.4.0 — the highest MINIMAL version that satisfies everyone — no surprise upgrades, no diamond conflicts.

The go.sum file: cryptographic hashes of the dependency content — every module's downloaded content is verified against go.sum before use. It's not a lock file (it doesn't select versions — go.mod does); it's the integrity check. Commit both go.mod and go.sum.
